test_path: (no dedicated unit test). One-time OAuth scaffold; htmlEscape is custom (not shared).

findings.failing_input: Adversary crafts URL: GET /api/oauth/tiktok/callback?state=javascript:alert(1) (or other novel injection vectors).
findings.expected: Defense against XSS in BOTH attribute contexts AND text contexts; ideally use a vetted helper or CSP.
findings.actual: Custom htmlEscape covers the 5 basic chars (ampersand, lt, gt, double-quote, single-quote) BUT the auth_code + state + error + errorDesc params are interpolated into both text content AND attribute contexts (e.g. inside a code tag or inside a style attribute value followed by greater-than). For attribute context the escaping is sufficient. However: no Content-Security-Policy header on any of the 4 HTML response paths. Combined with the lack of an X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header and no Referrer-Policy, a successful injection via a TikTok-side bug or DOM clobbering on a future change is unmitigated. Severity Major because OAuth callback endpoints are universally hardened with CSP per OWASP ASVS 5.0 V14.
findings.fix_sketch: Add response headers: `'Content-Security-Policy': "default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'", 'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff', 'Referrer-Policy': 'no-referrer'`. Inline styles are needed for the existing layout — `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` permits them while blocking script execution. Consider also `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.

findings.failing_input: Adversary GETs /api/oauth/tiktok/callback?auth_code=BENIGN&state=$(...crafted...) with no actual OAuth handshake.
findings.expected: Endpoint validates state against a server-stored CSRF nonce (or rejects if state empty / malformed).
findings.actual: state is reflected verbatim with no server-side verification. Comment says 'caller should set it to a CSRF nonce when constructing the auth URL and verify it matches in the rendered output' — but the verification is the OPERATOR'S manual eyeball check (Hebrew text on line 271). This is the documented OAuth scaffold pattern; URL-obscurity + manual exchange flow mitigates. NOT a flag under operator constraints (single-operator URL-obscurity), but should be documented in the audit.
findings.fix_sketch: Acknowledged limitation. If TikTok production OAuth is wired in a follow-up phase, store nonce server-side and compare here.

findings.failing_input: Operator copies the curl command verbatim and runs it.
findings.actual: <YOUR_APP_ID> and <YOUR_APP_SECRET> placeholders use angle-brackets that render correctly. No issue.

uncertainty_notes: Endpoint is documented Phase 05.7.5-B scaffold. URL-obscurity trust model accepted for inner routes, but OAuth callbacks are external-facing by definition (TikTok cloud redirects browser here). CSP/security headers gap is genuine; under operator-baseline this is Major.
test_coverage_gaps: Zero coverage. Recommend ONE smoke test for the security headers (CSP + nosniff + Referrer-Policy) + ONE test that htmlEscape correctly escapes & < > " ' in attribute context.
htmlEscape duplicated (only call site) — fine as-is.
